slots.brief: A circular loop of changing radius in a uniform magnetic field; ask for the induced emf as a function of time via dΦ/dt (no figure needed).
Ball thrown vertically upward from a height; ask for time to reach ground using two kinematic equations (no figure).
A wire is stretched so its length increases by a given fraction at constant volume; ask for the new resistance in terms of the original.
A cell of given emf and internal resistance connected across an external resistor; ask for terminal voltage or power dissipated (no figure).
Diagram of a particle at a point with position and velocity vectors marked; ask for the angular momentum of the particle about the origin using r × mv.
Circuit diagram of a capacitor network with a battery; ask for the charge on a specific capacitor after series-parallel reduction.
Diagram of two springs connected to a mass (series/parallel arrangement); ask for the time period of SHM using the equivalent spring constant.
At a place, the angle of dip and the horizontal component of Earth's field are given; ask for the vertical component or total field strength.
A block released from rest on a smooth track slides down and compresses a spring; ask for maximum compression using energy conservation (no figure).
An object placed at a distance from a concave mirror produces an image with given magnification; ask for the focal length using mirror formula and magnification relation.
Given the equation of a progressive wave y = A sin(kx − ωt), ask the student to read off amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed.
YDSE diagram with slits and screen geometry; ask for the number of fringes visible in a region or the fringe width from given slit-screen distance.
Light passing through two thin prisms in contact for zero net deviation; ask for the required relation between angles and refractive indices (dispersion without deviation).
A source and observer moving toward each other on a straight line; ask for the ratio of the apparent frequencies in approach and recede cases.
Two waves superpose with a given phase difference and intensities; ask for the resultant intensity at a point (no figure needed).
P–V diagram of a cyclic process (rectangle/triangle in P–V plane); ask for the net work done per cycle as the enclosed area.
A solid floats at the interface of two immiscible liquids with different densities; ask for the fraction of volume in each liquid using buoyancy balance.
Given a trajectory equation y = ax − bx², ask for the time of flight and horizontal range by comparing with the standard projectile form.
Compare the rms speeds of two gases at the same temperature given their molar masses; ask for the ratio (simple scaling).
A hot body cools in a room; given cooling data over one interval, ask for its temperature after another equal interval using Newton's law of cooling.
A potential function V(x, y) is given; ask for the electric field components by differentiating V, then the magnitude at a point.
Ice at 0°C is mixed with water/steam; ask for the final equilibrium temperature accounting for latent heat (calorimetry with phase change).
The period of a pendulum is measured with given percentage errors in length and time; ask for the percentage error in g using the pendulum formula.
A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at an oblique angle; ask to show/identify that the path is a helix and find its pitch or radius (easy direct formula).
A man in an accelerating lift with a weighing scale; ask for the scale reading given the lift's acceleration (pseudo-force framing).

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: A square loop or regular polygon wire carrying current is placed near a finite straight wire; ask for the net magnetic field at the centre using superposition.
An electron in a hydrogen-like atom/species absorbs a photon of given energy; ask which excited state it reaches and what transitions are possible on de-excitation.
A wire of given length and area is loaded within elastic limit; using Young's modulus relation, ask for elongation or breaking load, possibly with two loading conditions to solve.
Circuit diagram of a Zener diode in reverse bias across a load with a series resistor and unregulated supply; ask for current through the Zener or load voltage.
Diagram of a system of charges or a non-uniform charge distribution (e.g., charged sphere, shell, or cavity); ask for field at a point using Gauss's law with symmetry arguments.
Two planets of given radii and mean densities; ask for the ratio of acceleration due to gravity at their surfaces using g ∝ ρR.
A satellite's orbit radius is changed from r1 to r2; ask for the work done using the change in total orbital energy (−GMm/2r).
A block on a rough horizontal surface is pulled by a force inclined at an angle to the horizontal; ask for the acceleration or the minimum force to just move it (symbolic/numeric).

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: Light of given intensity/area falls on a surface (absorbing/reflecting); ask for the radiation pressure or force using momentum flux of EM waves.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slots.brief: An electron and a proton (or alpha particle) accelerated through the same potential difference; ask for the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths.
A radioactive sample has a given half-life; ask for the fraction/mass remaining after a specified number of half-lives (simple counting).
A person standing on a freely rotating platform folds their arms (moment of inertia changes); ask for the new angular velocity using angular momentum conservation (no figure).
In a series LCR circuit at a given frequency, ask for the phase difference between current and voltage, or state whether current leads or lags (easy direct reasoning).
Circuit diagram showing a combination of logic gates (e.g., NAND gates); ask for the output logic expression or complete truth table for all inputs.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: A metal of given work function is illuminated with light of a given wavelength; ask whether emission occurs and if so, find the stopping potential via the photoelectric equation.

Given a compound formula, ask the student to compute the oxidation state of a specific element in it and then compare it with a second compound — a figure showing the structural formula of both compounds for reference.
Ask which among a set of 4 common drugs (aspirin, paracetamol, ibuprofen, morphine) is used as an analgesic and antipyretic but not anti-inflammatory — direct fact recall.
Four statements about diagonal relationship / reactions of Ca and Mg compounds — e.g. thermal decomposition of CaCO3 vs MgCO3, solubility of sulfates down the group — pick the incorrect one.
Pick the correct reagent from 4 options to convert a phenol to an aryl ether / to cleave a given aryl alkyl ether under controlled conditions.
Given three ions, ask which has the maximum number of unpaired electrons with a brief reason via electronic configuration.
Energy of a hydrogen-like species at a given n — ask to find the orbit/series transition producing a given ratio of energies (use the fact E ∝ Z^2/n^2).
Describe a positive carbohydrate/sugar test without naming the test — ask the student to identify which test from the description.
Figure showing phenol treated with dilute HNO3 vs concentrated HNO3 — ask for the product(s) and a comparison of mononitration vs picric acid formation.

slots.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slots.brief: Given three alkenes (or their heats of hydrogenation), ask which is most/least stable — a typical ranking MCQ with reasoning via substitution.
For a strong electrolyte vs weak electrolyte in water, ask to identify the correct molar-conductivity trend statement — conceptual MCQ with the dissociation explanation embedded.
Real vs ideal gas conceptual — under what conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behaviour, given the van der Waals constant assumptions — one-line conceptual answer.
Four statements about adsorption (freundlich isotherm exponent range, physisorption vs chemisorption at low/high temperature, and why adsorption is exothermic) — pick the incorrect one.
Ratio of de Broglie wavelengths of two particles (e.g. an alpha particle and a proton) accelerated through the same potential difference — numerical answer using λ ∝ 1/√(mq).
Given a first-order reaction where concentration drops from x to x/16 in a time t, ask how long for x to x/32 — integer multiple of half-lives.
Four statements on tropospheric vs stratospheric pollution (NOx role, ozone depletion, photochemical smog); pick the incorrect one.
How many octahedral and tetrahedral voids per atom in fcc; 4 options with the correct count relationship.
Give XeF2, XeF4, XeF6 and ask which are square planar / which have lone pairs on the central atom — count lone pairs via VSEPR and match to shapes.
Given a balanced combustion equation of a liquid hydrocarbon, compute Δn_g (gaseous moles products minus reactants) and then apply ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT for the numeric answer.
A figure showing a Williamson synthesis setup — given R-X and R'-ONa, ask the student to pick the correct ether product and explain why the reverse pairing (halide from the hindered group) fails.
Four given orders (e.g. ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, atomic radius, electronegativity) — pick the one that is INCORRECT for the specified set of elements.
Simple percentage composition → empirical formula problem: given % of C, H and O (or just two elements + oxygen by difference), ask the empirical formula or the simplest whole-number ratio.
Ask the student to identify the correct naming of a given complex, or pick which ligand is bidentate / which complex is paramagnetic.
Given ΔH° and ΔS° for a reaction, compute ΔG° and the equilibrium temperature at which it becomes spontaneous — numeric via ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.

Given a di- or trisubstituted carbonyl compound (figure with structure), ask for all correct tests/reactions it will show — codes like (i) Tollens positive, (ii) Cannizzaro positive, (iii) iodoform positive, etc.
Given the electronic configuration of a lanthanide/transition ion, compute its spin-only magnetic moment using √(n(n+2)) BM.
Given a structure described in text (e.g. a substituted cycloalkene or a chain with halogen and OH), pick its correct IUPAC name — standard nomenclature with one correct and three near-miss options.

4 statements on buffer/Le Chatelier applied to a described equilibrium — identify the correct set; keep it a two-statement (Assertion-Reason style) question on shifting an exothermic equilibrium with temperature/pressure change.
Which compound has the highest/lowest lattice enthalpy from a set of ionic compounds (e.g. NaF vs NaCl vs KCl etc.) — ordering-style comparison MCQ.
Four reagents listed for a given substrate transformation — three accomplish it, one does not; identify the odd one out.
Given a 3-step conversion from benzene to a substituted amine (e.g. nitration → reduction → diazotisation → substitution), ask which reagent sequence achieves it — 4 multi-reagent options.
Given the cell notation of a spontaneous cell at 298 K, ask which is the cathode / direction of electron flow / sign of ΔG — conceptual reasoning about E°cell without heavy computation.

Ask which of the given mixtures will show positive/negative deviation from Raoult's law, or what the vapour composition will be above a given liquid mixture — conceptual with a numeric percentage or a qualitative pick.
Two statements — one on directional properties of hybrid orbitals, one on a specific molecule's shape (e.g. of BeCl2 in gas vs solid phase) — pick the correct combination option.
For a sparingly soluble salt, given Ksp and molar solubility, ask for the solubility in g/L or in a common-ion medium — moderate numeric with ICE-table style reasoning.
Column I has 4 organic reactions/species, Column II has mechanisms/stability ranks/products — ask for the correct matching set.
Given a complex ion (with ligands listed), determine its hybridisation/geometry/spin state using CFT — figure-free but with structural formula of the complex in the question.
Complete the reaction: diborane with water / with LiH / with HCl — pick the products of a given diborane reaction.
Four statements about NH3 vs other group-15 hydrides (boiling point anomaly, bond angle trend, thermal stability down the group, reducing character) — pick the incorrect one.
Which of the listed isomers are not resonating / which species is aromatic by Hückel's rule — e.g. rank or pick the aromatic one among cyclopentadienyl anion, cycloheptatrienyl cation, etc.
Single-blank sentence using a simple contextual clue (e.g., weather/behaviour) with four common adjectives; correct answer inferable directly from context.
Four/five-sentence paragraph on a familiar topic (travel or science) with one clear opening sentence and a chronological/logical chain; ask for correct order.
Give a common idiom (e.g., 'to let the cat out of the bag') embedded in a short sentence; choose the option closest in meaning.
Complex sentence layering subject-verb agreement, tense and a preposition; the subtle trap should be in agreement/idiom usage, with 'No error' as a genuine plausible option.
Simple two-word analogy pair (e.g., 'Doctor : Hospital') with four analogous pairs; all four options should be recognisable noun-profession/place relations.
Short sentence with a time clause; the error tests wrong present tense with 'since/for' or after time conjunction; three parts are grammatically clean.
Five-sentence jumble where the first and last sentences are given; the middle three must be ordered using pronoun/connector references.
Give a moderately literary word in a short sentence; four synonym options of similar register, with only one exact match (others slightly off in nuance).
Ask for the synonym of a word used in a sentence; correct answer should be a common word, distractors are related but not equivalent in meaning.
Double-blank sentence with subtle clue contrast (e.g., 'despite her ___ demeanour, her ___ ambition'); both blanks must agree logically, distractors should fit only one blank.
Ask the antonym of a simple, high-frequency word (e.g., 'generous' or 'brief') presented in isolation; four straightforward options.
Preposition gap-fill: choose the correct preposition in an idiomatic phrase (e.g., 'conform to', 'consist of'); distractors are common misused prepositions.
Sentence divided into three parts (a), (b), (c); the verb immediately after a preposition is wrongly in base form instead of gerund; other parts are error-free.
letter pair analogy where each letter shifts by a fixed positional value; ask for the analogous pair among options, with a mixed-letters distractor
odd-one-out where four items share a category but one differs on a secondary attribute (function or type); all common words, no number patterns
pointing-style relation chain: a person points to a photo or describes a chain of relations; ask how the target person is related to the speaker
arrange four related words into a logical/chronological sequence and identify which option gives the correct order
letter-shift code: a word is coded by shifting each letter by a constant value or reversing position; apply the same rule to decode/coding a new word
alpha-numeric or mixed series with two interleaved components (letters following one rule, numbers another) where one term is wrong; identify the incorrect term
two statements followed by conclusions; pick the conclusion that definitely follows (no possibility-type conclusions)
shortest distance between two given skew lines; test coplanarity first, then apply the distance formula
simplify a composite like sin⁻¹(x) + cos⁻¹(x) or tan⁻¹(x) + cot⁻¹(x) inside a nested expression using standard identities
decide intervals where a simple polynomial/rational function is increasing or decreasing by testing the sign of f′(x)
evaluate a determinant whose rows share terms, using row operations to pull out a common factor and split into simpler determinants
use f(a+x) = f(a−x) symmetry (or King's property) on a definite integral to reduce it to a standard result
find the term independent of x in a single binomial expansion by setting the exponent of x in the general term to zero
given an ellipse with specified a and b, compute eccentricity and/or foci using the standard relations
find the foot of perpendicular from a given point to a given line using the standard projection/ratio formula
evaluate an indefinite integral that reduces cleanly with a substitution such as t = tan x or t = √(linear)
determine k so that a non-homogeneous 3×3 system has infinitely many solutions by enforcing Δ = 0 with a consistent numerator determinant
solve a first-order linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) after identifying and applying the integrating factor

slots.subtopic: Cross product and angle between vectors
slots.brief: compute the cross product of two given vectors, then use it to find the sine of the angle between them (or the area of the triangle they span)
for a small grouped dataset, compute mean deviation about the median through a step-by-step table
a piecewise function with an unknown constant at a joint; find k by equating left and right limits for continuity/differentiability
verify/compute a vector triple product expression like a×(b×c) or (a×b)×c, possibly testing whether a given identity holds
use differentials to approximate the value of a function (e.g. a root or a power) at a nearby point
find the complete general solution of a trigonometric equation reducible to a single function via factorisation or double-angle formulae
evaluate a definite rational/trig integral with the Weierstrass substitution t = tan(x/2), changing limits accordingly
compute |z| or 1/z-type expressions combining conjugates, e.g. simplify z·z̄ and (1/z) rewritten via conjugate over modulus squared
condition for a line to be tangent to a circle: substitute the line into the circle and set discriminant to zero to find the unknown parameter
count 4-digit numbers formed from given digits satisfying a divisibility (e.g. by 5) or position restriction, splitting into disjoint cases

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: find the image of a given point in a given line using the perpendicular-foot/reflection formula
solve a homogeneous first-order DE by substituting y = vx, separating variables and integrating
integrate a proper rational function using partial fractions (distinct linear factors) via the cover-up technique
find absolute maximum/minimum of a function on an interval or of a parameterised expression via derivative tests and endpoint values
classical probability of a simple event (dice, cards, balls) by counting favourable over total outcomes
use the onto-function counting formula (inclusion–exclusion) to count surjections from an m-set onto an n-set
compute the area between a curve (parabola/line) and the x-axis or between two curves by direct integration of given intersection limits
find the domain of a function involving a square root and a denominator; decide via inequalities/intersection of conditions
compute cardinalities of A∪B, A∩B etc. from given |A|, |B|, |A∩B| using inclusion–exclusion
sum the first n terms of an arithmetico-geometric series using the shift-and-subtract (difference) method
given a quadratic with roots α, β, evaluate a non-trivial symmetric expression (e.g. α³+β³ or α²β+αβ² type) using Vieta's relations without solving
given two groups' sizes, means and variances, compute the combined mean and combined variance using the standard formulas
given a constraint among angles of a triangle (or A+B+C = π), prove/derive a conditional trig identity via sum-to-product manipulations and pick the matching option
find the equation of tangent and normal to an implicitly defined curve (e.g. x²+xy+y² = c) at a given point via implicit differentiation
find the argument (and quadrant) of a given complex number, possibly after multiplying by a conjugate or simplifying a product
evaluate a limit of the form (sin kx)/(sin ax) or (1−cos)/x² type using standard trigonometric limits
count arrangements/selections with at least one condition satisfied using total minus the complementary count
given focus and directrix (or vertex plus axis) of a parabola, construct its equation in standard form

slots.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slots.brief: find coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line in 3-space using vector projection
find the range of a rational function y = f(x) by converting to a quadratic in x and imposing discriminant ≥ 0
two-stage Bayes' theorem problem: given prior probabilities and likelihoods, compute the posterior probability of a cause given the observed outcome
statement-based MCQ on symmetric/skew matrices: which of the given expressions (e.g. A+Aᵀ, AAᵀ, A−Aᵀ) is always symmetric or skew-symmetric
check coplanarity of three vectors (or points) via the scalar triple product / determinant being zero and find the missing parameter
binomial distribution: compute P(X = k) or the mean/variance given n and p using the standard formulas
